display.title: Rosh Chodesh Av: The Head of the Month
display.summary_short: Why the first day of the month is called Rosh Chodesh, the 'head', how the whole month draws its blessings from it, and the Shabbos Mevarchim prayer before Rosh Chodesh Av.
display.summary_long: A short talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show before Rosh Chodesh Av. Uncle Yossi explains that 'Rosh' does not mean new but head: just as the head guides and gives life to the whole body, the first day of the Jewish month is linked to every other day. On Rosh Chodesh Hashem grants the blessings of health, life and livelihood, food, clothing and shelter, which are then shared out over the month, so we say special prayers and take extra care with our behavior. Some people visit the resting places of tzaddikim on Erev Rosh Chodesh, where prayers are especially accepted. On Shabbos Mevarchim, the Shabbos before Rosh Chodesh, we ask Hashem for a month of life and peace, joy and gladness, and especially, this Av, for Moshiach and the redemption, our only true consolation; and we all answer Amen.
display.lesson: Rosh Chodesh is the head of the month: begin each month with prayer and good behavior, because the whole month draws its blessings from it.
